title: Prime ideals and contractions of regular components in an étale stalk
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $D\hookrightarrow X$ be a reduced closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-reduced-scheme], and let $(D_a)_{a\in F}$ be its distinct reduced irreducible components, indexed by a finite set $F$ [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Assume every $D_a$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let $v:W\to X$ be étale [def-weil-etale-morphism], let $w\in W$, put $x=v(w)$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $R=\mathcal O_{W,w}$, and write $\varphi:A\to R$ for the stalk map [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Let $I\subseteq A$ be the ideal of $D$ and $F_x=\{a\in F:x\in D_a\}$. For $a\in F_x$ let $\mathfrak p_a\subseteq A$ be the ideal of $D_a$ and put $\mathfrak q_a=\mathfrak p_aR$. Then the $\mathfrak p_a$ are exactly the distinct minimal primes over $I$; $\mathcal O_{D_a,x}=A/\mathfrak p_a$; and the closed pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $D_a\hookrightarrow X$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathfrak q_a)$. Each $R/\mathfrak q_a$ is a nonzero regular local domain, each $\mathfrak q_a$ is a proper prime, and $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_a)=\mathfrak p_a$. In particular the $\mathfrak q_a$ are distinct. With $V(J)$ denoting the set of primes containing an ideal $J$ in $R$, one has $V(IR)=\bigcup_{a\in F_x}V(\mathfrak q_a)$, including the empty-family case. Components missing $x$ have empty pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}R$.

proof.text: Choose a Noetherian affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing $x$, using [pqf-def-locnoeth]. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-irreducible-closed-correspondence], the nonempty $D_a\cap U$ are exactly the distinct irreducible components of $D\cap U$: the order-preserving correspondence preserves maximal irreducible closed subsets. Their reduced structures are the restrictions of those on $D_a$, since reducedness is a local-ring condition [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Apply [lem-sfb-closed-component-stalk-calculus] to the reduced closed subscheme $D\cap U$ of the Noetherian scheme $U$. Stalks are unchanged by restriction to a neighborhood. It gives exactly the distinct minimal primes $\mathfrak p_a$ over $I$, the quotient descriptions $\mathcal O_{D_a,x}=A/\mathfrak p_a$, and $I=\bigcap_{a\in F_x}\mathfrak p_a$. A component missing $x$ has unit stalk ideal. The empty intersection is $A$.

For $a\in F_x$, apply [lem-trf-finite-intersection-etale-stalk-model] with the single closed subscheme $D_a$ and $z=x$. It identifies $D_a\times_X\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathfrak p_aR)$ and the local ring at the unique point $\widetilde w$ of $E_a=D_a\times_XW$ over $w$ with $R/\mathfrak p_aR$. Its natural stalk map is $A/\mathfrak p_a\to R/\mathfrak p_aR$. The local Noetherian hypothesis and the condition $x\in D_a$ required there both hold.

The projection $E_a\to D_a$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-stalk-invariants] at $\widetilde w$: its target stalk $A/\mathfrak p_a$ is regular local by regularity of $D_a$ and [def-weil-regular-scheme], so its source stalk $R/\mathfrak q_a$ is regular local, and the quotient stalk map is faithfully flat. By [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] this quotient is a nonzero integral domain. Therefore $\mathfrak q_a$ is a proper prime: a product lies in $\mathfrak q_a$ exactly when the product of its classes in the quotient is zero.

For each $a\in F_x$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] to the faithfully flat map $C=A/\mathfrak p_a\to S=R/\mathfrak q_a$ and the $C$-module $C$. Under $C\otimes_C S\cong S$, $c\otimes s\mapsto cs$ with inverse $s\mapsto1\otimes s$, its injectivity says that $A/\mathfrak p_a\to R/\mathfrak q_a$ is injective. Thus $\varphi(b)\in\mathfrak q_a$ if and only if $b\in\mathfrak p_a$, giving the stated contraction. Equal $\mathfrak q_a$ would have equal contractions and hence equal indices by Step 1.

Let $Q$ be any prime of $R$. Then $IR\subseteq Q$ if and only if $I\subseteq\varphi^{-1}(Q)$. If $F_x$ is nonempty, Step 1 gives $\prod_{a\in F_x}\mathfrak p_a\subseteq I$; primality forces $\mathfrak p_a\subseteq\varphi^{-1}(Q)$ for some $a$. Indeed, otherwise choose one element of each $\mathfrak p_a$ outside that prime; their product contradicts primality. This condition is equivalent to $\mathfrak q_a\subseteq Q$. Conversely $I\subseteq\mathfrak p_a$ gives $IR\subseteq\mathfrak q_a$. This proves $V(IR)=\bigcup_{a\in F_x}V(\mathfrak q_a)$. If $F_x$ is empty, Step 1 gives $I=A$, hence $IR=R$ and both sides are empty.

proof.text: Finally let $a$ miss $x$. On the affine neighborhood $U$ of Step 1, write $D_a\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J_a)$ using [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its unit stalk ideal says $J_aA=A$, so $J_aR=R$. Apply [lem-sbc-finite-affine-tensor-base-change] with a singleton family $E_0=B/J_a$ and $B$-algebra $R$. The pullback is $\operatorname{Spec}((B/J_a)\otimes_B R)$. The explicit quotient isomorphism sends $(b+J_a)\otimes r$ to $\varphi_B(b)r+J_aR$, with inverse $r+J_aR\mapsto(1+J_a)\otimes r$. Thus its ring is $R/J_aR=0$ and its spectrum is empty. Restriction to $U$ computes the original pullback since $\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ factors through $U$.
